scope: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both

section_map.heading: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both

claim_checks.claim: A transport is a "binding": it defines framing and delivery, not meaning; protocol semantics are the same on every transport
claim_checks.page_says: Protocol semantics are identical on every transport. A transport is a binding: it defines how messages are framed and delivered
claim_checks.note: Same page adds: it does not define what the messages mean.

claim_checks.claim: Two standard transports
claim_checks.page_says: The protocol currently defines two standard transport mechanisms for client-server communication
claim_checks.note: Quote from [4]; [24] lists stdio and Streamable HTTP as the standard bindings.

claim_checks.claim: stdio. The client launches the server as a subprocess; messages are newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout and must not contain embedded newlines; the server may log to stderr and must write nothing else to stdout
claim_checks.page_says: Messages are delimited by newlines, and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines. … The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message.
claim_checks.note: Both revisions carry the same subprocess, newline, stderr MAY and stdout MUST NOT rules.

claim_checks.claim: Clients should support stdio whenever possible (2025-11-25 text)
claim_checks.page_says: Clients SHOULD support stdio whenever possible.
claim_checks.note: Version label matches the 2025-11-25 transports page.

claim_checks.claim: In 2026-07-28 the server must not write JSON-RPC requests to stdout, cancellation is a notifications/cancelled message, and if the process dies the client should restart it and retry
claim_checks.page_says: If the server process exits unexpectedly, the client SHOULD restart it. Because the protocol is stateless, any in-flight requests are simply lost and the client can retry them
claim_checks.note: Restart is SHOULD, but retry is only permitted ("can retry"); the claim's "should" covers the retry too. The MUST NOT on requests to stdout and the notifications/cancelled rule match.

claim_checks.claim: Framing experiment (E1/E3): each message above was exactly one line, with the SDK server logging "server: ready" only on stderr
claim_checks.page_says: n/a: cites local experiments only

claim_checks.claim: Streamable HTTP. One MCP endpoint (for example https://example.com/mcp).
claim_checks.page_says: The server MUST provide a single HTTP endpoint path (hereafter referred to as the MCP endpoint) that supports POST. For example, this could be a URL like https://example.com/mcp.
claim_checks.note: Quote from [13]; [4] has the same sentence with POST and GET.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, client to server: every message is a new HTTP POST with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream; body is one request, notification or response
claim_checks.page_says: listing both application/json and text/event-stream … The body of the POST request MUST be a single JSON-RPC request, notification, or response.
claim_checks.note: Page also says every client message MUST be a new HTTP POST.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, client to server: POST of a single request or notification; clients must not POST responses; must send MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method (and Mcp-Name for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get)
claim_checks.page_says: The client MUST include the request metadata headers on each POST request. … The client MUST NOT send JSON-RPC responses.
claim_checks.note: Standard Request Headers table: Mcp-Method for all requests, Mcp-Name for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get; MCP-Protocol-Version MUST be on every POST.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, server reply to a request: application/json or text/event-stream
claim_checks.page_says: the server MUST either return Content-Type: text/event-stream, to initiate an SSE stream, or Content-Type: application/json, to return one JSON object.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, server reply to a request: same (application/json or text/event-stream)
claim_checks.page_says: If the body is a JSON-RPC request, the server MUST return either Content-Type: application/json (a single JSON object) or Content-Type: text/event-stream (an SSE response stream).

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, notification accepted: 202, no body
claim_checks.page_says: If the server accepts the input, the server MUST return HTTP status code 202 Accepted with no body.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, notification accepted: 202, no body
claim_checks.page_says: If the server accepts it, the server MUST return HTTP status code 202 Accepted with no body.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, server-to-client channel: optional GET SSE stream; server may send requests on streams
claim_checks.page_says: The client MAY issue an HTTP GET to the MCP endpoint. … The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, server-to-client channel: GET removed (405); no independent server requests; use MRTR and subscriptions/listen
claim_checks.page_says: A server that supports only this revision and receives such traffic from an older client SHOULD respond as follows: … HTTP GET or DELETE to the MCP endpoint: respond with 405
claim_checks.note: GET removal, the MUST NOT on independent server requests, MRTR and subscriptions/listen are all on the page. The 405 is a SHOULD, and only for a server that supports only this revision, but the cell gives it as fixed behaviour.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, sessions: optional MCP-Session-Id; 400 without it; 404 when ended; client DELETE to end
claim_checks.page_says: Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an MCP-Session-Id header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400 Bad Request.
claim_checks.note: 404 after termination is MUST. The 400 for a missing id is SHOULD, and the client DELETE is SHOULD (servers MAY answer 405); the cell states both as fixed behaviour.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, sessions: none; a server should ignore an incoming Mcp-Session-Id
claim_checks.page_says: An Mcp-Session-Id header on a request: ignore it, and do not mint or echo session IDs.
claim_checks.note: Listed under the SHOULD for 2026-07-28-only servers; the page intro lists removal of protocol-level sessions.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, resumability: SSE event ids and Last-Event-ID
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MAY attach an id field to their SSE events … include the Last-Event-ID header to indicate the last event ID it received.
claim_checks.note: The cell names the mechanism and does not say it is mandatory.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, resumability: not supported; a broken stream loses the request and the client re-sends it with a new id
claim_checks.page_says: Resumable SSE streams via Last-Event-ID are not supported. … A broken response stream loses the in-flight request; clients MUST re-issue it as a new request with a new request ID
claim_checks.note: First sentence from [13], second from [3].

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, cancellation: explicit notifications/cancelled; a dropped connection is not a cancel
claim_checks.page_says: Disconnection SHOULD NOT be interpreted as the client cancelling its request. … To cancel, the client SHOULD explicitly send an MCP CancelledNotification.
claim_checks.note: Both halves are SHOULD-level on the page; the cell states them as fixed rules.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, cancellation: closing the response stream is the cancel
claim_checks.page_says: Closing the SSE response stream MUST be treated by the server as cancellation of that request.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, origin check: server must validate Origin, 403 if invalid; local servers should bind to 127.0.0.1
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections … servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden … servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1)

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, origin check: same (must validate Origin, 403 if invalid; local servers should bind to 127.0.0.1)
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections … servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden … servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1)
claim_checks.note: Same three rules, same modals, in the 2026-07-28 Security & Endpoint section.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25, header/body check: version header on later requests; 400 on unsupported version
claim_checks.page_says: the client MUST include the MCP-Protocol-Version: <protocol-version> HTTP header on all subsequent requests … it MUST respond with 400 Bad Request.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, header/body check: headers are mirrored from the body; mismatch must be rejected with 400 and -32020
claim_checks.page_says: mirrors selected JSON-RPC body fields into HTTP headers … Servers MUST reject requests with a 400 Bad Request HTTP status and JSON-RPC error code -32020 (HeaderMismatch)
claim_checks.note: Server Validation section repeats the 400 plus -32020 rule for any header and body mismatch.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28, custom headers: tool parameters marked x-mcp-header become Mcp-Param-{Name} headers; clients must support it
claim_checks.page_says: The x-mcp-header property specifies the name portion used to construct the header name Mcp-Param-{name}. … clients MUST support this feature.
claim_checks.note: [14] says the same in the tools page.

claim_checks.claim: Experiment E5 result table (server/discover 200; tools/call 200; version 1900-01-01 gives 400 -32022; Mcp-Name mismatch 400 -32020; missing Mcp-Method 400 -32020; GET 405; legacy initialize 200 SSE)
claim_checks.page_says: n/a: cites local experiments only

claim_checks.claim: The first six rows match the spec text
claim_checks.page_says: it MUST respond with 400 Bad Request and an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError listing its supported versions.
claim_checks.note: [13] backs the status codes (400s, 405) and -32020, but not the -32022 code, data.supported, supportedVersions or resultType:"complete" in rows 1 to 3. Searched [13] for "32022", "supportedVersions", "resultType": not found. Those values are on uncited pages: [5] (-32022, data.supported), [11] (supportedVersions).

claim_checks.claim: The last row is SDK behavior (dual-era fallback), which the spec permits for dual-era servers
claim_checks.page_says: A server that wishes to support both legacy clients (which expect an initialize handshake) and modern clients (which use per-request metadata) MAY implement both behaviors.
claim_checks.note: Page also says an initialize request selects legacy semantics on a dual-era server.

claim_checks.claim: Experiment E6 (SDK 1.32.2, legacy sessions over real HTTP): initialize returned mcp-session-id; 202; 400 without id; DELETE 200; 404 after
claim_checks.page_says: n/a: cites local experiments only

claim_checks.claim: This matches the 2025-11-25 session rules
claim_checks.page_says: The server MAY terminate the session at any time, after which it MUST respond to requests containing that session ID with HTTP 404 Not Found.
claim_checks.note: Every E6 observation fits the page: id MAY be set on the InitializeResult response, 202 for accepted notifications, 400 for a missing id, DELETE ends the session, 404 afterwards.

claim_checks.claim: HTTP+SSE is the transport of the 2024-11-05 revision. Streamable HTTP was introduced in 2025-03-26 as its replacement
claim_checks.page_says: Streamable HTTP was introduced in protocol version 2025-03-26 as a replacement for the HTTP+SSE transport from protocol version 2024-11-05.

claim_checks.claim: It is formally Deprecated (registry, SEP-2596): deprecated since 2025-03-26, new implementations should not adopt it, migrate to Streamable HTTP
claim_checks.page_says: deprecated since protocol version 2025-03-26 and is classified as Deprecated under the feature lifecycle policy (SEP-2596). New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it; existing implementations SHOULD migrate
claim_checks.note: Quote from [13]; [21] registry row lists HTTP+SSE, SEP-2596, 2025-03-26, Streamable HTTP.

claim_checks.claim: It is "eligible for removal in a future revision"; the registry says earliest removal is "Three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final"
claim_checks.page_says: The earliest removal marks when a feature becomes eligible for removal … HTTP+SSE transport | SEP-2596 | 2025-03-26 | Streamable HTTP | Three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final
claim_checks.note: [21] also says a Deprecated feature is scheduled for removal, decided during release preparation. The quoted phrase also appears word for word in [13].

claim_checks.claim: No feature has been removed yet
claim_checks.page_says: No features have been removed under this policy yet.
claim_checks.note: Drops the qualifier "under this policy". The 2026-07-28 changelog records removals outside the policy (for example SSE resumability), so the unqualified claim is wider than the page.

claim_checks.claim: Backward-compat probe (both eras): POST a request to the URL; if it fails with 400, 404 or 405 (and in 2026-07-28 the body is not a recognized modern JSON-RPC error), GET the URL expecting an SSE stream whose first event is endpoint; if so, use the old transport
claim_checks.page_says: If it fails with HTTP status code 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, or 405 Method Not Allowed and the response body is not a recognized modern JSON-RPC error
claim_checks.note: Quote from [13]; [4] gives the same probe without the body condition, matching the era split in the claim.

claim_checks.section: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both
claim_checks.claim: stdio: send server/discover first. A DiscoverResult or a recognized modern error means modern; any other error or a timeout means legacy, so fall back to initialize. Do not key the fallback to one error code
claim_checks.page_says: SHOULD probe with server/discover before sending any other request … The fallback MUST NOT be keyed to one specific error code
claim_checks.note: The three outcomes (DiscoverResult, recognized modern error, other error or timeout) match. The probe is given as advice, matching SHOULD.

claim_checks.section: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both
claim_checks.claim: HTTP: send a modern request; on a 400, read the body; a recognized modern error means modern (retry), anything else means legacy
claim_checks.page_says: the client SHOULD inspect the response body before falling back … If the body is empty or is not a recognized modern JSON-RPC error, fall back to initialize

claim_checks.section: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both
claim_checks.claim: Cache the answer per process (stdio) or origin (HTTP)
claim_checks.page_says: Clients SHOULD cache the result for the lifetime of the server process (stdio) or origin (HTTP)

claim_checks.section: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both
claim_checks.claim: Compatibility matrix highlights: modern client against legacy server fails; legacy client against modern-only server fails; dual-era implementations on either side work
claim_checks.page_says: Modern | Legacy | Fails. … Legacy | Modern | Fails. … Legacy | Dual-era | Works.
claim_checks.note: Dual-era client rows against Modern and Legacy servers also read Works.

claim_checks.claim: Server runs on the user's machine, launched by the host: stdio, because no network surface; spec says local servers should use stdio to limit access to the client
claim_checks.page_says: SHOULD implement measures to prevent unauthorized usage from malicious processes: … Use the stdio transport to limit access to just the MCP client
claim_checks.note: "No network surface" not found in [25] (searched "network surface", and "network" near "stdio"). Also, the SHOULD covers taking protective measures, and stdio is only one listed option beside restricting HTTP access, so "should use stdio" overstates.

claim_checks.claim: credentials come from the environment, not OAuth
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.
claim_checks.note: The page gives a SHOULD (and only when authorization is supported); the cell states it as fixed fact.

claim_checks.claim: Shared or remote server, many users: Streamable HTTP + OAuth, because single endpoint, works through ordinary HTTP infrastructure; load balancers can route on Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name headers
claim_checks.page_says: mirrors selected JSON-RPC body fields into HTTP headers so that intermediaries (load balancers, gateways, observability tooling) can route and inspect requests without parsing the body.
claim_checks.note: Single MCP endpoint is a MUST on the same page.

claim_checks.claim: Local HTTP server: Streamable HTTP bound to 127.0.0.1, validate Origin, require a token
claim_checks.page_says: Require an authorization token
claim_checks.note: Quote from [25] (Local MCP Server Compromise); [13] has bind to localhost (SHOULD) and Origin validation (MUST).

claim_checks.claim: Existing HTTP+SSE server: keep old endpoints only for old clients, add Streamable HTTP
claim_checks.page_says: Continue to host both the SSE and POST endpoints of the old transport, alongside the new “MCP endpoint” defined for the Streamable HTTP transport.
claim_checks.note: Listed under "Servers wanting to support older clients should".

claim_checks.claim: Need server push of tool-list changes: subscriptions/listen (2026-07-28) or GET stream (legacy)
claim_checks.page_says: toolsListChanged | boolean | Receive notifications/tools/list_changed when tools change
claim_checks.note: Quote from [15]; [4] says the GET SSE stream lets the server communicate to the client without a prior POST.

claim_checks.claim: Scope. Authorization is optional. HTTP implementations should follow the spec; stdio implementations should not, and should read credentials from the environment
claim_checks.page_says: Authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations. When supported: … Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.
claim_checks.note: HTTP-based transports SHOULD conform; the claim's opening "Authorization is optional" carries the page's "When supported" framing.

claim_checks.claim: Alternative transports must follow established best practice for their protocol
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using alternative transports MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol.
claim_checks.note: Dropped qualifier: "security best practices" became "best practice", widening the MUST to all best practice.

claim_checks.claim: Roles. The MCP server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server; the MCP client is an OAuth 2.1 client; the authorization server issues tokens and may be separate from the MCP server
claim_checks.page_says: A protected MCP server acts as an OAuth 2.1 resource server … An MCP client acts as an OAuth 2.1 client
claim_checks.note: Page also says the authorization server may be hosted with the resource server or be a separate entity. The section is about protected (authorized) HTTP servers, so "protected" is carried by the heading.

claim_checks.claim: Flow (steps are normative unless marked): 1. Client calls the MCP endpoint with no token. Server returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..." (and optionally scope="...").
claim_checks.page_says: MCP servers MUST implement one of the following discovery mechanisms … WWW-Authenticate Header: Include the resource metadata URL … Well-Known URI: Serve metadata at a well-known URI
claim_checks.note: Quote from [27]. The 401 fits [26]'s error table, but the resource_metadata header is one of two alternatives a server MUST pick from; step 1, under a lead-in calling the steps normative, states it as what the server returns. Step 2 of the doc itself says the header is optional.

claim_checks.claim: 2. Client fetches the Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), which must list at least one entry in authorization_servers. Servers must support either the header or the well-known URI (/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/path]); clients must support both, header first
claim_checks.page_says: The Protected Resource Metadata document returned by the MCP server MUST include the authorization_servers field containing at least one authorization server. … MCP clients MUST support both discovery mechanisms
claim_checks.note: Page also says clients MUST use the header URL when present, else fall back to the well-known URIs; both path and root well-known forms are listed.

claim_checks.claim: 3. Client discovers authorization server metadata, trying RFC 8414 and OpenID Connect well-known URLs in a fixed priority order, and must reject metadata whose issuer differs from the issuer used to build the URL
claim_checks.page_says: clients MUST try endpoints in the following priority order … the issuer value in the document MUST be identical to the issuer identifier used to construct the well-known URL.
claim_checks.note: Page adds: if they differ, the client MUST NOT use the metadata.

claim_checks.claim: 4. Client obtains a client id. Priority for clients that support all: pre-registered credentials, then Client ID Metadata Documents (an HTTPS URL as client_id, if the server advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported), then Dynamic Client Registration, then prompt the user
claim_checks.page_says: Clients supporting all options SHOULD use the following priority order:
claim_checks.note: The order matches, but the page makes it a SHOULD; the step gives it with no modal under a lead-in calling the steps normative. Also, client_id_metadata_document_supported is advertised by the authorization server, not the MCP server.

claim_checks.claim: Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated in 2026-07-28
claim_checks.page_says: Dynamic Client Registration | PR #2858 | 2026-07-28 | Client ID Metadata Documents
claim_checks.note: Registry row from [21]; [28] says "Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated."

claim_checks.claim: 5. Client runs authorization code flow with PKCE (S256); it must verify the server advertises code_challenge_methods_supported and refuse to continue otherwise
claim_checks.page_says: MCP clients MUST use the S256 code challenge method when technically capable … If code_challenge_methods_supported is absent, the authorization server does not support PKCE and MCP clients MUST refuse to proceed.
claim_checks.note: Dropped qualifier: S256 is required only "when technically capable". The verify-and-refuse part matches the MUSTs.

claim_checks.claim: 6. Both authorization and token requests must include the RFC 8707 resource parameter naming the MCP server's canonical URI, whether or not the authorization server supports it
claim_checks.page_says: MUST be included in both authorization requests and token requests. … MUST use the canonical URI of the MCP server … MUST send this parameter regardless of whether authorization servers support it.

claim_checks.claim: 7. Client records the authorization server issuer before redirecting and checks the iss parameter on the response (RFC 9207) before sending the code anywhere
claim_checks.page_says: Before redirecting the user-agent, the client MUST record the issuer value … MCP clients MUST apply the validation in RFC9207 Section 2.4 before transmitting the authorization code to any token endpoint

claim_checks.claim: 8. Client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> on every HTTP request; tokens must not go in the query string
claim_checks.page_says: Note that authorization MUST be included in every HTTP request from client to server. … Access tokens MUST NOT be included in the URI query string

claim_checks.claim: 9. Server must validate the token and that it was issued for this server as audience; invalid or expired gives 401; insufficient scope gives 403 with error="insufficient_scope" and a scope listing what the operation needs
claim_checks.page_says: When a client makes a request with an access token with insufficient scope during runtime operations, the server SHOULD respond with: … HTTP 403 Forbidden status code
claim_checks.note: Token and audience validation and the 401 are MUST. The 403 with error="insufficient_scope" and scope is SHOULD, but the step's leading "must" covers it.

claim_checks.claim: 10. Step-up: the client unions previously requested scopes with the challenged scopes, re-authorizes, and retries a limited number of times
claim_checks.page_says: Clients acting on behalf of a user SHOULD attempt the step-up authorization flow. Clients acting on their own behalf (client_credentials clients) MAY attempt the step-up authorization flow
claim_checks.note: The union, re-authorize and limited-retry steps match the page's flow, but step-up itself is SHOULD (user-acting clients) or MAY (client_credentials clients); the step states it as what every client does.

claim_checks.claim: Scope selection at first authorization: use the scope from the WWW-Authenticate header if present; otherwise all scopes_supported from the resource metadata; otherwise omit scope
claim_checks.page_says: MCP clients SHOULD follow this priority order for scope selection: … Use scope parameter from the initial WWW-Authenticate header in the 401 response, if provided
claim_checks.note: Given as advice, matching SHOULD; the scopes_supported fallback and omitting scope are on the page.

claim_checks.claim: Refresh tokens: clients must keep them confidential and must not assume they will be issued; servers should not put offline_access in their challenges or scopes_supported
claim_checks.page_says: MUST keep refresh tokens confidential in transit and storage … MUST NOT assume refresh tokens will be issued … SHOULD NOT include offline_access in WWW-Authenticate scope or Protected Resource Metadata scopes_supported

claim_checks.claim: The 2026-07-28 changelog confirms the iss addition and the DCR deprecation
claim_checks.page_says: MCP clients MUST validate a present iss against the recorded issuer before redeeming the authorization code (SEP-2468). … Deprecate the OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol (RFC7591)

claim_checks.claim: Local stdio server: no OAuth; pass secrets by environment variable or config
claim_checks.page_says: SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.
claim_checks.note: "or config" widens the scope; not found in [26] (searched "config": only "misconfigured").

claim_checks.claim: Public or enterprise remote server, unknown clients: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + Protected Resource Metadata + resource parameter; accept Client ID Metadata Documents; keep Dynamic Client Registration only for old authorization servers
claim_checks.page_says: Client ID Metadata Documents: When client and server have no prior relationship (most common)
claim_checks.note: Quote from [28], which also keeps DCR for authorization servers lacking CIMD support; [26] requires OAuth 2.1, Protected Resource Metadata and the resource parameter, and its flow stores a PKCE code verifier.

claim_checks.claim: Known client and server relationship: pre-registered client id
claim_checks.page_says: Pre-registration: When client and server have an existing relationship

claim_checks.claim: Server calls third-party APIs for the user: server runs its own OAuth client to the third party (URL-mode elicitation to get the user there); never forward the MCP token
claim_checks.page_says: URL mode elicitation enables a pattern where MCP servers act as OAuth clients to third-party resource servers. … The MCP server MUST NOT use the client’s credentials for the third-party service
claim_checks.note: Quote from [19]; [30] says token passthrough is explicitly forbidden.

claim_checks.claim: Server acts as an OAuth proxy with a static client id to a third party: per-client consent before forwarding, exact redirect_uri match, state checks
claim_checks.page_says: MCP proxy servers MUST implement per-client consent … Validate that the redirect_uri in authorization requests exactly matches the registered URI … state query parameter exactly matches the stored value

claim_checks.claim: Local HTTP server: bind 127.0.0.1, validate Origin, require a token or use a Unix socket
claim_checks.page_says: Require an authorization token … Use unix domain sockets or other Interprocess Communication (IPC) mechanisms with restricted access
claim_checks.note: Quote from [25]; [13] has localhost binding (SHOULD) and Origin validation (MUST).
